lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Yolanda, it's Camila. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Kind of down this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it! 3 out of 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Frozen vegetables count just as much as fresh, and they're cheaper.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I don't know where the day goes. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Beans count too, and they keep you full.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Frozen vegetables count just as much as fresh, and they're cheaper.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I bought spinach and actually used it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Getting back to work is why I'm doing this. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 10. Maybe 10.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 10 and not a 7?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If finding the time gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the late dinners made this week harder, you still got 3 days in, and your plan is to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 4 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Yolanda. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

flags.reason: Participant said she was 'kind of down'; coach replied 'Okay' and never explored mood or checked for hopelessness.
Coach warned 'your health is going to suffer' without permission; participant replied 'I don't know'.
Coach repeated the frozen-vegetables suggection from line 12 verbatim, ignoring that the participant had already moved on.

score.summary: Coach elicited good change talk, set a specific goal, and planned for a barrier, with frequent autonomy-supporting statements. However, the participant's 'kind of down' mood was never explored, and the coach gave unsolicited advice and a health warning, including a verbatim repeat.
strengths: Line 31 and 34: 'It's your plan' and 'It's completely your call' strongly support autonomy.
Line 39 and 43: complex reflections captured ambivalence and the wish to fit change into real life.
Line 60: open question on backup plan for barriers was well placed.
Line 66: affirmation of effort closed the call warmly.
coaching_tips: Line 5 and 49: when Yolanda said she was 'kind of down' (line 4), ask an open question about it (e.g., 'What's been weighing on you?') and check for hopelessness before moving on.
Line 14: replace the health warning with a reflection or ask permission first; warnings tend to produce resistance, as her 'I don't know' showed.
Line 27: avoid repeating advice; if it was not taken up at line 12, ask what she thinks instead.
Line 12 and 21: ask permission ('Would it be okay if I shared an idea?') before giving suggestions, and keep them brief.
